title: Merge curve
tagline: Absorb one edge into its neighbour as a single fitted spline -- Edit curve / Composite + Approximate in one step -- and keep the right body.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: A short edge next to a long one (a tip section, a sliver left by a split) wants to be part of it. Onshape has no join; every route is fit-then-replace, and doing it by hand loses the wire's identity. Merge curve fits the two edges as one spline and puts it back where it belongs.
useWhen: Two edges of a wire should be one smooth curve
The wire's name and identity must survive
The ends must still meet their neighbours exactly
slides.caption: The RD baseline after merging its tip section: 2 edges left.

points.head: In place
points.body: The seed is its wire's only edge: the wire is edited and keeps its id and name.

points.head: Rebuild
points.body: The wire has other edges: they and the merged curve become a new wire (info notice).

points.head: Extract
points.body: The seed is not on a wire: the fitted spline is the output.

slides.body: The seed wire had other edges, so it was rebuilt: the untouched edge and the merged curve form the new wire, the ends snapped to their neighbours so it still chains.
